messages:
maria_cust: Hey support — seeing a consistent issue where iOS Safari clients drop mid-stream (SSE) when users switch from WiFi to cellular or lock/unlock the phone. App v1.3.4. Users get partial output and the UI never recovers. Have screenshots and a couple request IDs. Anyone seen mobile Safari do this?

alex_support: Sorry you're hitting this, Maria. Can you paste one of the request IDs + approximate timestamps? Also, quick repro steps if you have them.

maria_cust: Sure — request_id=rx-8f3b2c1a, first seen ~2026-03-09T21:12:04Z. Repro steps we used:
1) Open chat in iOS Safari (not in-app webview)
2) Start a long streamed completions (>= 120s)
3) While stream is coming, lock the phone or flip from office WiFi to cellular (AirDrop wifi switch or toggle wifi)
4) Unlock or finish switch — stream is gone, UI shows partial text and never reconnects.

client logs we see:
```
EventSource.onerror -> TypeError: Failed to fetch
// or sometimes
network error: connection aborted
```
No 500s on client, just failure in EventSource.

alex_support: Thanks — pinging eng-runtime to look at server-side connection logs around rx-8f3b2c1a. Also, do you observe any 4xx/499 from our edge LB? Any proxied error codes in your logs?

rowan_eng-runtime: re: rx-8f3b2c1a — pulled logs, here are relevant snippets from our edge (trimmed):
```
2026-03-09T21:12:04Z connection_id=cn-72a3 req=rx-8f3b2c1a method=POST path=/v1/stream status=200 duration_ms=120345 stream_open=true
2026-03-09T21:13:05Z connection_id=cn-72a3 client_closed reason=RST_STREAM error_code=0
2026-03-09T21:13:05Z connection_id=cn-72a3 stream_closed_by_client partial_bytes=8423
```
Looks like the client reset the TCP/TLS connection (RST_STREAM), server had produced ~8.4KB of stream. No 5xx.

rowan_eng-runtime: Two immediate thoughts:
- The browser / iOS may kill background TCP connections on network change without firing a reconnect event for EventSource.
- Our fronting LB (AWS ALB / Cloudflare-like) has an idle timeout and might be closing connections when the client pauses; when the client resumes it doesn't always open a new EventSource in the app if the page didn't reload.

alex_support: Tess from SRE — can you check LB idle timeouts and any connection churn around that timestamp?

tess_eng-sre: Looking now. For the region that rx-8f3b2c1a hit, the ALB idle timeout is 60s. I can see a pattern: when the client backgrounded the phone, there's ~70s gap in TCP activity then a RST on resume. Example snippet from LB: 
```
2026-03-09T21:12:00Z target_conn=tc-19 idle=0
2026-03-09T21:12:45Z target_conn=tc-19 idle=45
2026-03-09T21:13:05Z target_conn=tc-19 timeout_close reason=idle_timeout
```
So LB is closing the connection (idle_timeout) slightly before the client tries to reuse it, and the client-side EventSource sees a network failure but doesn't auto-retry in this scenario.

tess_eng-sre: Quick workaround we can try on our side: bump ALB idle timeout to 120s for streaming endpoints and set `proxy_read_timeout` higher in the NGINX sidecar. That will reduce the chance of LB-initiated closes while mobile briefly goes offline or pauses. I'll open a canary config change.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for config change: increase streaming idle_timeout -> 120s in region eu-west-1. Canary target: 5% of traffic.

maria_cust: Appreciate it. Is there anything we should change on client side as immediate mitigation?

rowan_eng-runtime: Yes — for SSE/EventSource specifically:
- Ensure clients handle `onerror` and try to re-create the EventSource with exponential backoff. Some iOS Safari instances silently swallow reconnects if the page wasn't interacted with, so explicitly re-instantiating helps.
- As a server-side compatibility trick we can send SSE comment keepalives (a single colon-line) every 15–30s to keep the connection active: `: keepalive\n\n`. Browsers generally treat comments as no-op but they reset idle timers.
- If you can change to a WebSocket in the app (in-app webview or native), that tends to behave better across network changes.

alex_support: Rowan — is there any security or infra downside to sending frequent SSE comments from the runtime? Bandwidth cost?

rowan_eng-runtime: Bandwidth is negligible (a few bytes per keepalive). Main cost is maintaining longer-lived connections — this affects connection concurrency limits on the runtime and GPUs remain unaffected since tokens are produced only when requested. We should make the keepalive opt-in per route or toggleable per customer to avoid unnecessary global load.

tess_eng-sre: Canary looks healthy so far. No increased 5xx, connections honored. If canary stays green for 30m we'll roll to 50% then 100%.

maria_cust: Quick note from a mobile engineer on our side: we tried re-instantiating EventSource on `visibilitychange` (when document.hidden toggles) and that helped some cases but causing a flicker and duplicate partial content in others. Ideally we'd resume without a full re-request. Any resume token support in Redwood?

rowan_eng-runtime: We don't currently support resume semantics for SSE streams (no byte-offset resume), that's something the product/roadmap team has discussed as a feature. Short-term: dedupe client-side UI by tracking message ids or a `last_event_id` header — EventSource supports `Last-Event-ID` to hint server which events were seen. If you can include a `Last-Event-ID` on re-open we can skip duplicates server-side.

alex_support: Product takeaway — add a small note to docs about mobile Safari behavior + recommended client-side patterns (visibilitychange -> re-open, keepalives, WebSocket fallback). Also add guide to toggle LB timeout for streaming-heavy customers.

rowan_eng-runtime: Filed infra task: RD-STREAM-1423 "SSE keepalive opt-in for streaming endpoints" to implement server-side periodic comments and a customer flag. Also created RD-PLAT-1424 for adding docs and example client-side code.

maria_cust: Thanks — one last ask: after you roll the LB timeout change and the canary is full, can you DM me or drop a note here so we can validate in our staging with the same network switch tests? We'll also try the `visibilitychange` re-open approach with `Last-Event-ID` to minimize dupes.

tess_eng-sre: Will do. Canary finished and rolled to 100% at 2026-03-09T21:46Z. Change: ALB idle_timeout -> 120s for streaming route.

deploy-bot: Deployment success: config-streaming-timeout updated in eu-west-1 -> 100% at 2026-03-09T21:46:37Z. :white_check_mark:

maria_cust: Confirmed in staging: network switch repro is much less frequent now, still seeing a couple of cases where the client never attempts a reconnect automatically on Safari. Implementing client re-open and `Last-Event-ID` reduced duplicates. Thanks everyone.

alex_support: Great — marking this thread as resolved for now but keeping RD-STREAM-1423 open until keepalive opt-in is done. If you hit anything new ping us and we can escalate. :thumbsup:

rowan_eng-runtime: Quick dev tip to include in docs snippet for teams:
```js
// client-side visibility handler
document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', () => {
  if (!document.hidden) {
    if (!es || es.readyState === EventSource.CLOSED) {
      // re-create EventSource, pass Last-Event-ID if available
      es = new EventSource('/v1/stream?session=abc', { withCredentials: true });
      if (lastEventId) es.headers = { 'Last-Event-ID': lastEventId };
    }
  }
});
```
This isn't perfect (iOS quirks) but it's a practical mitigation until we ship resume support.

maria_cust: We'll try that. Thanks for quick turnaround and the canary. Appreciate the thorough logs and the LB change.

alex_support: Thanks everyone. Closing the user escalation — follow-ups tracked in RD-STREAM-1423 and RD-PLAT-1424.
